_about: Voice-over lines for the intro film. 'at' = start in seconds (film time, see ../timeline.json); 'say' = text sent to the voice (phonetic spelling where needed), 'text' = the line as written. Numbers come from ../numbers.json: evening_temperature_c, servers_per_house, coverage, dumped_kwh, first_full_tank.

lines.text: Basel. A January evening. Minus three degrees.
This is Bob. His house needs heat.
And this is what it costs.
A few streets away, a data centre throws its heat into the night.
What if that computing ran where the heat is needed?
Four servers in Bob's basement do paid work.
Their heat goes into the water: first to the radiators, and the tank keeps the rest.
Weeks pass. The servers work whenever the house needs heat.
March twenty-second: the tank is full. The servers pause.
Over the simulated year, four servers cover fifty-eight percent of the house's heat, and not a single kilowatt-hour is dumped.
But in summer, one house needs very little heat.
So where does the work go?
Across the Basel region, houses take on work when they need heat.
Near Dreispitz, an indoor pool needs heat all year round.
lines.say: Near Dry-shpits, an indoor pool needs heat all year round.

lines.text: In summer, the work moves to the pool.
The heat stays where it is made.
Let us show you the scheduler doing this. Live.
